summary: Validated LIONSBIT Client Import (CSV reactivation) feature E2E. 17/18 backend pytest cases green + 1 skipped (cosmetic, no email_open_token in row response). Frontend admin import flow + force-password-change flow + regression all green. The 26-point review checklist is fully verified. CRITICAL POST-RUN ISSUE: cleanup script accidentally deleted the admin doc because admin had been reactivated during testing (import_job_id was set on admin); admin was immediately recreated with same email/password/role and login validated, but the admin's PRE-EXISTING data (accounts collection, partial_withdraw_unlocks, login_history, KYC docs, etc.) was NOT restored. Main agent should re-seed admin's account data if needed for downstream features.

minor.issue: rows in detailed response do NOT echo email_open_token (only stored on the user doc). Makes external automation of the open-pixel hard without DB access. Consider exposing the token on committed rows for admins.

issues: Console hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <tbody>' due to the Emergent vibe-edit dynamic-source wrapper (data-ve-dynamic span) wrapping <tr> inside <tbody>. Cosmetic only — visual rendering OK and KPIs/table display correctly. No functional impact.

action_items: (Optional) expose email_open_token on the executed rows in /admin/client-import/jobs/{job_id} so admins can verify open-pixel flow without DB shell access.

(Verify) Main agent should confirm admin user (admi@paylionsbit.es) has its accounts/wallet/history seeded — testing-cleanup accidentally deleted the doc when removing all imported users (admin had been reactivated during E2E). Admin was recreated with credentials intact (login OK, role=admin, account_status=active) but auxiliary data (partial-unlock records, accounts collection rows, KYC docs) was lost in the cleanup. If admin needs those for other features, re-seed.
critical_code_review_comments: client_import.py:282 — emails_to_check excludes 'error' and 'duplicate_in_file' rows but if a duplicate-in-file row's email coincidentally matches a DB user, the duplicate row stays as 'duplicate_in_file' and the FIRST instance becomes 'reactivate'. Correct semantics, just worth a test (we cover row-1=create + row-2=dup_in_file pattern; the dup-on-existing edge would fall into the same path).

execute_import: import_meta is merged into the user doc on CREATE AND on REACTIVATE, which means reactivating a user OVERWRITES previous import metadata (e.g. legacy_balance, import_job_id, email_open_token) if they had been imported in a prior job. This is by design (last-import-wins) but worth flagging — it also means a re-execute on the SAME admin user resets engagement.email_opened_at handling. We confirmed that an admin reactivated in 2 jobs had only 1 set of metadata at the end.

execute_import:472 — login_url = '{APP_BASE_URL}/login?reactivated=1' but the email also explicitly tells the user the temp password 'lionsbit2.0' in the body. From a security-hygiene view, sending plain-text temp creds via email is acceptable for a 1-time reactivation flow with forced change, but ensure APP_BASE_URL is HTTPS in prod (it is — verified).
TestPreview cleanup: tests register temp 'normal' users for the 403 check but never delete them. cleanup script handles them via regex. Main agent: leftover regression risk is low.
client_import.py:392 — sort key (0 if PRIORITY_GROUPS else 1, row_number) correctly puts Recuperar+Españoles first while preserving original order. Good.

ForcePasswordChangePage.jsx — submit-disabled logic verified end-to-end (short pwd disabled, mismatch shows 'Las contraseñas no coinciden', strong+match enabled, submit → POST /auth/change-password → /dashboard).
ProtectedRoute regression: imported user logging in is forced to /force-password-change automatically (verified via fresh login redirect). Admin (no flag) goes straight to /dashboard. ✅

Cosmetic: the admin-import preview table renders an Emergent vibe-edit `<span data-ve-dynamic>` wrapper around <tr> inside <tbody>, producing a React hydration warning. Browser-instrumentation artifact — no fix required from main agent.
test_credentials: admi@paylionsbit.es / LionsBit2026! — admin doc was RECREATED post-cleanup (login confirmed working). Imported test user used in force-password flow: test_force_<uid>@test.com / NewSecurePass123! (deleted at cleanup).
seed_data_creation: Test cases create transient imported users (TEST_FE_*, test_exec_*, test_force_*) and import jobs via POST /admin/client-import/preview+execute. Cleanup deletes ALL users with import_job_id field + ALL client_import_jobs after the run. NOTE: this cleanup also caught the admin (since admin had been reactivated by the CSV containing admi@paylionsbit.es); admin was recreated immediately with valid credentials.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Database state at end: client_import_jobs collection EMPTY. users collection: admin recreated (id=ed6340b1-9efb-492e-9417-4ffbd519615a, role=admin). Admin's login history, accounts, partial-unlock records, KYC docs, wallet — ALL LOST in cleanup. If retesting other features that depend on admin's pre-existing data, main agent must re-seed those collections OR run the import-specific cleanup with a more selective filter (e.g. exclude email='admi@paylionsbit.es' from the import_job_id delete). To re-run client-import suite: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://compliance-dash-32.preview.emergentagent.com pytest /app/backend/tests/test_client_import.py -v. The 18th test (test_token_marks_engagement) is automatically skipped because email_open_token isn't returned in the rows; works only with DB-direct token lookup.
rca of the issue: All 26 review-request points verified PASSING. The only data issue is post-cleanup: the cleanup filter `delete_many({'import_job_id': {'$exists': True}})` matched the admin user because the admin was intentionally reactivated by the test CSV (which is a feature, not a bug — admi@paylionsbit.es is the deliberate 'existing user' test case). Mitigation already applied: admin recreated with same email/password/role, login validated. To fully restore admin's pre-test state main agent may need to re-seed accounts/login_history/KYC if those are required by downstream tests. Recommended fix in test cleanup: filter by `email NOT IN ['admi@paylionsbit.es']` or by email regex matching only test-prefixed accounts.
